la:noun:alvus.html:
alvus, i, f. (m., Att. ap. P.; 718 ib., and ; Calv., Ael. Cin., and Laber. ap. P.) [for aluus from alo: venter feminae ab alendo dicta, Paul. ex Müll. and so Varr.; acc. to others kindr. with Sanscr. ulvam = uterus, and this again connected with vulva, volvo; ἐλύω εἰλύω; Sanscr. val = to turn; O. H. Germ. wallen = to roll],
the belly, the paunch, the bowels.
Lit.: purgatio alvi,: forsitan purgat alvum,; ; cf. : solvere,: exonerare,: inanire, et saep.: non descendit alvus,is costive,: cui satis alvus reddit cotidie,, n. 2: alvus cita,active,: alvum bonam facere,: movere,: citare,: adstringere alvum,to make costive,; so also: cohibere, comprimere, supprimere, firmare, sistere, inhibere, etc., to bind, constipate, etc.—In plur.: ad eliciendas alvos,.—Hence, for excrement: alvus varia,: alvus liquida, nigra, pallida, pinguis,; and for flux, diarrhœa: alvus corpus ac vires carpit, .—
Transf.
The womb: in alvo gestare,; twice in Cic.: cum praegnans Dionysium alvo contineret,: spes in alvo commendata,; so ; —
The stomach, the digestive organs, ; so ; .—
A beehive (very freq.): mediā alvo, quā introeant apes,: alvi melle plenae,: si plenae alvi fuerint,: (apes) alvo se continent,; ; ; so .—
Of the basin of the molten sea in the Jewish temple: (boves) alvum maris circuibant,.

senses: hollow, deep vessel, basket, trough, tray; deep cavity, excavation
la:noun:alveus.html:
alvĕus, i, m. (alveum, n., ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. naustibulum, p. 169 Müll.) [alvus],
a hollow, a cavity.
In gen.: vitiosae ilicis alveo,.—
Esp.
A hollow, deep vessel, a basket, trough, tray; also, a deep cavity, excavation, : in alveo,: fluitans alveus,; : alveus scrobis,—
The hold or hull of a ship: alveos navium,: alvei navium quassati,.—Hence (pars pro toto), a small ship, a boat, skiff: cavatus ex materiā alveus,: accipit alveo Aeneam,.—
A hollowed gaming-board, Varr. ap. : alveus cum tesseris lusorius,; : alveo et calculis vacare,, n. 2.—
= alvus and alvearium, a beehive (in Pliny, alvus (Jan), q. v. II. C.): gens universa totius alvei consumitur,; so ; ; .—
A bathing-tub: in balneum venit ... ut in alveum descenderet, etc., Auct. ad ; .—
The channel or bed of a river: fluminis alveo,; : fluminis Ritu feruntur, nunc medio alveo Cum pace delabentis etc.,: nec quisquam citus aeque Tusco denatat alveo, Müll. (not elsewhere): pleno alveo fluere,: alveo navigabile perfodere angustias,i. e. a canal,: per crepidinem alvei,: reversae sunt aquae in alveum suum,

senses: a small gaming board upon which the dice are thrown
a small channel of a river
